history.heading: Great Moravia and Hungary
paragraphs: Slavs settled the region of present-day Slovakia in the 5th and 6th centuries. In the 9th century it was part of Great Moravia, where Saints Cyril and Methodius introduced Christianity and the first Slavic script. After Great Moravia fell in the early 10th century, the territory became part of the Kingdom of Hungary for about a thousand years.

After the Ottomans conquered central Hungary in the 16th century, Bratislava (Pozsony) became the Hungarian capital and coronation city until 1830. Mining towns such as Banská Štiavnica were among the richest in Europe.

history.heading: Czechoslovakia
paragraphs: A Slovak national revival in the 19th century, led by figures such as Ľudovít Štúr, codified the Slovak language. In 1918 Slovakia joined the Czech lands to form Czechoslovakia. In 1939, under Nazi pressure, a Slovak state led by Jozef Tiso was created as a German satellite; it deported tens of thousands of Jews. The Slovak National Uprising of 1944 rose against it.
After the war Czechoslovakia became communist. Slovak Alexander Dubček led the Prague Spring of 1968, crushed by a Warsaw Pact invasion. The Velvet Revolution of 1989 ended communism.

history.heading: Independent Slovakia
paragraphs: Slovakia became independent peacefully on 1 January 1993 after the "Velvet Divorce" from the Czech Republic. It joined NATO and the EU in 2004 and adopted the euro in 2009. The 2018 murder of investigative journalist Ján Kuciak and his fiancée prompted mass protests. In 2024 Prime Minister Robert Fico survived an assassination attempt.

culture.heading: Traditions
paragraphs: Slovak is a West Slavic language closely related to Czech. Most Slovaks are Catholic, and there is a significant Hungarian minority in the south and a Roma minority. Slovakia has many castles, including Spiš Castle, one of the largest in Central Europe and a UNESCO site.
Folk traditions include the fujara, a large shepherd's flute recognised by UNESCO. Bryndzové halušky (potato dumplings with sheep cheese) is the national dish. Ice hockey is the most popular sport.

politics.heading: Parliamentary republic
paragraphs: Slovakia is a parliamentary republic with a directly elected president and a prime minister leading the government. Robert Fico's Smer party returned to power in 2023. Critics, including the EU, have raised concerns about changes to criminal law, the media and NGOs, and the government has taken a softer line on Russia, prompting large protests.

economy.heading: Car manufacturing
paragraphs: Slovakia produces more cars per person than any other country in the world, with plants of Volkswagen, Kia, Stellantis and Jaguar Land Rover; Volvo is building one too. Electronics, machinery and metals are also important. The economy is highly dependent on the automotive industry and exports. The currency is the euro.
